title: How the day closed
text: Stocks slipped on Tuesday. SPY fell 0.4% and QQQ fell 0.7%. The big story was an inflation report that came in hotter than expected, plus a second rough day for NVIDIA. Not everything went down, though. Industrial companies had the best day of any sector, and Broadcom, TSMC, Lockheed Martin and Rocket Lab all closed higher. A mixed day like this is a good reminder that one headline rarely moves every stock the same way.

title: Prices rose faster than expected in October
text: The government said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, a bit more than the 0.3% that experts had guessed. News reports say this makes it more likely that the Federal Reserve raises interest rates in December. Higher rates make borrowing cost more, and that can weigh on fast growing tech stocks. The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, the highest level in the last 12 months.

title: NVIDIA falls for a second day
text: NVIDIA dropped 5.5% to about $168.80. It is now 31% below its 52 week high and only about 3% above its 52 week low of $164.27. The drop came after news reports raised questions about the CEO, and the company's board started its own review. NVIDIA still reports its quarterly results on November 17, so more big moves are possible.

title: Rocket Lab climbs after record sales
text: Rocket Lab rose 6.5% to $62.71 after it reported record quarterly sales of $268 million, up 73% from a year ago. Remember that Rocket Lab has the highest risk score on our list, 10 out of 10. It is still about 58% below its 52 week high, which shows how far and how fast this kind of stock can swing.

title: Lesson 45: What is key person risk?
text: Some companies depend a lot on one leader, often the founder or CEO. Key person risk is the chance that something happening to that one person hurts the whole company. It could be health, a scandal, or the person leaving. When investors worry about a leader, the stock can fall even if the company's products and sales have not changed at all. That is what we saw with NVIDIA this week. Good companies try to lower this risk by building a strong team and a clear plan for who would take over. It is one more reason why owning many companies, not just one, can help.
